This name has been used in various historical contexts, including as the name of a palace in Spain built by the sultan Yusuf ibn Tashfin during the Islamic Almoravid Dynasty. The name "Alhambra" is a corrupted version of "Al-Hazariya," which means "the abode of the conqueror."
